data.name: Pauline
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin 'Paula', which is a feminine form of 'Paul'. In the Bible, Paul is a male name derived from the Latin word 'paulus', which means 'small' or 'humble'. Pauline is a name given to honour Paul, who was a prominent disciple of Jesus and wrote many letters in the New Testament.

in_hebrew.name: פאולין
in_hebrew.meaning: השם פאולין נגזר מהשם פאולוס ופירושו קטן או צנוע
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פאולין מקורו בשם פאולוס, שפירושו קטן או צנוע. השם פאולוס נגזר מהלטינית והוא קשור לאפוסטל פאולוס, אחד מהשליחים החשובים ביותר של ישו. האפוסטל פאולוס היה אישיות מרכזית בכתבי הברית החדשה והשם שלו הפך לסמלה של צניעות ומסירות. השם פאולין משמש כגרסה נשית של השם פאולוס ומשדר צניעות וקורבן עצמי.

in_greek.name: Παυλίνα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Παυλίνα σημαίνει μικρή ή ταπεινή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Παυλίνα προέρχεται από το όνομα Παύλος, που σημαίνει μικρός ή ταπεινός. Ο Απόστολος Παύλος ήταν κεντρική προσωπικότητα στα γραπτά της Καινής Διαθήκης και το όνομά του έγινε σύμβολο ταπεινώσεως και αυτοθυσίας. Το όνομα Παυλίνα είναι η θηλυκή μορφή του ονόματος Παύλος και αντανακλά τις ιδιότητες της σεμνότητας και του θυσιών.

in_latin.name: Paulina
in_latin.meaning: The name Paulina means small or humble
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Paulina is derived from the Latin name Paulus, meaning small or humble. The Apostle Paul, a central figure in the New Testament writings, bore this name. Paulina, as a feminine form of Paulus, embodies the virtues of modesty and self-sacrifice, reflecting the apostle's legacy of humility and devotion.

in_english.name: Pauline
in_english.meaning: The name Pauline means small or humble, symbolizing modesty
in_english.long_meaning: The name Pauline originates from the Latin name Paulus, meaning small or humble. It is associated with the Apostle Paul, a pivotal figure in Christianity and author of several New Testament epistles. The name Pauline, as a feminine derivative, conveys a sense of humility, modesty, and devotion. Historically, it has been used in various Christian cultures to signify a connection to these virtues and to the apostle's teachings. In modern usage, Pauline remains a popular name across different Christian denominations, symbolizing a spiritual legacy of selflessness and faith.

saint_reference.note: Several Christian saints have been named Pauline, reflecting the name's association with virtues of humility and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: Pauline is a name rooted in Christian tradition, resonating with the historical figure of Saint Paul, who played a significant role in spreading the teachings of Christianity throughout the Mediterranean world. His letters, often referred to as the Pauline Epistles, have shaped the theology and practices of Christianity to this day. The name Pauline connects its bearer to the rich legacy of faith and religious history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Pauline carries spiritual connotations, evoking the virtues of humility, devotedness, and faith that were embodied by Saint Paul. It is a reminder of the importance of following Christ's teachings and putting one's faith into action. In addition, the name draws attention to the responsibility of sharing God's word and spreading the message of salvation and love to others. Thus, Pauline represents not only a deep connection to religious tradition but also a call to live an impactful and spiritual life.

historical_references.reference: The Pauline epistles are a collection of letters attributed to Paul the Apostle in the New Testament of the Christian Bible. These letters were written primarily between AD 45 and 67, and provide evidence of the early Christian communities' beliefs, struggles and practices. The Pauline epistles are the third largest part of the New Testament, after the Gospels and the Acts of the Apostles.
historical_references.context: Early Christian communities in the Mediterranean world

historical_references.reference: Paul of Tarsus, later known as Paul the Apostle, was a Christian missionary and writer who is considered one of the most important figures in early Christianity. He was born in Tarsus, Cilicia around AD 5-10 and was educated in Jerusalem under the renowned Rabbi Gamaliel I. Paul's conversion to Christianity occurred around AD 33-35, and he became a leading figure in the spreading of the Christian message throughout the Mediterranean world. He was arrested in Jerusalem in AD 40, and was then taken to Rome where he was put on trial before Nero and was executed around AD 67.
